candidates: Giant Cell Tumor of Soft Tissue
key_facts: History of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma
Treated with 4 cycles of ABVC and 3060 cGY radiation
Previous excisions of left upper eyelid mass
Multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells on histopathology
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme
MRI shows lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment
Tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery
Extension into the right cavernous sinus and right sphenoid sinus with mass effect on the left temporal lobe
Genetic testing shows splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the PALB2 gene
champion: Giant Cell Tumor of Soft Tissue

raw.champion: Giant Cell Tumor of Soft Tissue
raw.rationale: The histopathology showing a multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, along with immunohistochemistry positive for CD68, is consistent with Giant Cell Tumor of Soft Tissue. The tumor's aggressive behavior, as evidenced by its rapid growth and extension into surrounding structures, also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman Disease
rejected.why: While Rosai-Dorfman Disease can also present with multinucleated giant cells, it typically involves the lymph nodes and has a distinct immunophenotype, including positivity for S100, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Primary Meningeal Melanoma
rejected.why: Primary Meningeal Melanoma would be expected to show melanocytic differentiation and positivity for melanocytic markers such as S100, which is not present in this case.
